problems.title: House Robber

cf.name: Boredom
cf.why: bucket equal values, then the no-two-adjacent DP over values

cf.name: Basketball Exercise
cf.why: two rows; consecutive picks must alternate rows

problems.gist: A night guard audits a row of storage lockers in a station. Locker i holds nums[i] rupees. Neighbouring lockers share one tamper sensor, so opening two adjacent lockers on the same night raises the alarm. Opening lockers that are not next to each other is safe.

problems.title: Coin Change

cf.name: Cut Ribbon
cf.why: unbounded knapsack; maximise pieces instead of minimising coins

problems.gist: You get an integer array coins of distinct coin values and an integer amount. You may use each coin value any number of times. Return the fewest coins whose values add up to exactly amount. If no combination makes that amount, return -1.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence

cf.name: Bubble Sort Graph
cf.why: the answer reduces to LIS length; needs O(n log n)

problems.gist: A climber logs the altitude at each checkpoint in an array nums. She wants to pick some checkpoints, keeping their original order (you may skip any, but never reorder), so that the chosen altitudes are strictly increasing.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs

gfg.t: Ways to Reach the n'th Stair

cf.name: k-Tree
cf.why: steps 1..k, count paths that use at least one step >= d

problems.gist: A staircase has n steps. Starting at the ground, each move climbs either 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of different sequences of moves that end exactly on step n. Two sequences are different if they differ in at least one move (so 1+2 and 2+1 count separately).

problems.title: Word Break
problems.gist: A label printer has dropped every space from a slogan, leaving one string s. You are also given a list wordDict of allowed words.

problems.title: House Robber II
problems.gist: A security tester checks the payment kiosks placed around a circular food court. Kiosk i holds nums[i] in cash. Because the kiosks form a circle, kiosk 0 and kiosk n - 1 are neighbours, as are kiosks i and i + 1.

problems.title: Edit Distance
problems.gist: A spell checker compares a typed word word1 with a dictionary word word2. It may change word1 using three operations, each costing one step:

problems.title: Unique Paths

gfg.t: Count Paths from Top Left to Bottom Right

problems.gist: A delivery robot stands on the top-left cell (0, 0) of a warehouse floor laid out as a grid with m rows and n columns. Its target is the bottom-right cell (m - 1, n - 1).

problems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
problems.gist: You are given two strings text1 and text2. Return the length of their longest common subsequence; return 0 if they have no common subsequence.

problems.title: Decode Ways
problems.gist: A message of capital letters was encoded with the mapping 'A' → "1", 'B' → "2", ..., 'Z' → "26", and the codes were written next to each other with no separator. Given the digit string s, return the number of ways to decode it back into letters.

problems.title: Palindromic Substrings
problems.gist: You are given a string s. Return how many of its substrings are palindromes. A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards; a substring is a contiguous, non-empty block of characters.

problems.title: Minimum Path Sum

gfg.why: 4-direction moves, so Dijkstra instead of DP

problems.gist: You are given an m x n grid of non-negative integers; grid[r][c] is the cost of entering cell (r, c). Start at the top-left cell (0, 0) and finish at the bottom-right cell (m-1, n-1). At every step you may move only one cell right or one cell down.

problems.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
problems.gist: You are given an array nums of positive integers (think of them as parcel weights). Decide whether the array can be split into two subsets with equal sums: every element goes into exactly one of the two subsets. Return true if such a split exists, otherwise false.

problems.title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
problems.gist: There are n jobs. Job i runs from startTime[i] to endTime[i] and pays profit[i]. Choose a set of jobs such that no two chosen jobs overlap in time, and return the maximum total profit.

problems.title: Burst Balloons
problems.gist: You get an array nums of n balloons; balloon i shows the number nums[i]. You must burst all of them, one at a time, in any order. Bursting balloon i earns nums[left] * nums[i] * nums[right] coins, where left and right are its current nearest unburst neighbours.

problems.title: Coin Change II
problems.gist: You get an integer amount and an array coins of distinct coin values, with an unlimited supply of each. Return the number of combinations of coins that add up to exactly amount. Two combinations are the same if they use the same count of every coin value (order does not matter).

problems.title: Target Sum
problems.gist: You are given an integer array nums and an integer target. Build an expression by writing either '+' or '-' in front of every number of nums (keeping their order) and joining them. For example, [3, 5] can give "+3-5" = -2.

problems.title: Unique Paths II
problems.gist: You get an m x n integer grid grid. A robot starts on the top-left cell grid[0][0] and wants to reach the bottom-right cell grid[m-1][n-1]. In one move it goes either one cell down or one cell right.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II

gfg.why: same task, asks for the buy/sell day pairs

gfg.t: Stock Buy and Sell – Multiple Transaction Allowed

problems.gist: You get an integer array prices where prices[i] is the price of one share on day i. On every day you may buy one share, sell the share you hold, or do nothing; you may hold at most one share at any time, and you may buy and sell on the same day.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III

gfg.t: Stock Buy and Sell – Max 2 Transactions Allowed

problems.gist: You get an array prices where prices[i] is the price of one share on day i. Find the maximum total profit you can make with at most two transactions. A transaction is one buy followed later by one sell.

problems.title: Interleaving String
problems.gist: Given strings s1, s2 and s3, decide whether s3 can be formed by interleaving s1 and s2.

problems.title: Maximal Square
problems.gist: You get an m x n matrix matrix whose entries are the characters '0' and '1'. Find the largest square sub-matrix that contains only '1's and return its area (side × side). If there is no '1', return 0.
